# Center for Aeronautical Studies (CEA - UFMG)
> High-performance experimental aircraft engineering laboratory at UFMG School of Engineering (Department of Mechanical Engineering - DEMEC). Pioneering German Akaflieg methodology in Brazil since 1963 and holder of 9 FAI World Speed and Climb Records.

## Core Capabilities & Mission
- **Experimental Aircraft R&D**: Full-lifecycle digital design, CFD aerodynamic optimization, FEA composite structural analysis, prototype fabrication, flight testing, and telemetry.
- **Academic Model**: German *Akaflieg* tradition ("Learning by Doing"), where engineering students design, build, and test real aircraft.
- **World Records**: 9 FAI (Fédération Aéronautique Internationale) world records held by CEA-308 and CEA-311 Anequim.
- **Industrial Co-Development**: R&D partnerships with aerospace leaders (Aeromot, Embraer) for sustainable aviation, bioethanol propulsion, and UAV systems.

## Main Resources & Pages
- [Home & Institutional Overview](https://cea.demec.ufmg.br/index.html): History, mission, laboratory infrastructure, technological matrix, and contact info.
- [Aircraft Projects & Fleet](https://cea.demec.ufmg.br/projetos.html): Technical specifications of Anequim (521 km/h), CEA-308, CB-2 Minuano, Gaivota CB-1, and active prototypes.
- [Technological Solutions & Services](https://cea.demec.ufmg.br/solucoes.html): CFD consulting, composite FEA calculations, flight test telemetry, and wind tunnel validation.
- [Founder Tribute - Prof. Cláudio Barros](https://cea.demec.ufmg.br/homenagem.html): Akaflieg philosophy pioneer, historical legacy, and design timeline.
- [Publications & Research Papers](https://cea.demec.ufmg.br/artigos.html): Peer-reviewed scientific output and technical flight test reports.
